newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was slow with the top price paid so far on Friday at $67.00 per cwt, steady with Thursday's light to moderate trade, feedlot sources said.

About 1,000 slaugher steers and heifers, that will likely grade select and choice, sold in Kansas. The week's USDA- confirmed sales there were 66,400 head, including 13,300 or about 20 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle.
About 700 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area Friday morning after weekly sales of 90,600 head, including 26,600 formulated and 2,100 contracted cattle.
Several feedlot managers said some owners continued to pass packer bids at $67.00 and were holding out for $68.00 amid expectations for higher beef prices next week.
Beef movement this week has been strong at sharply lower prices, fueling ideas that packers had cleaned out much of their inventory and would raise prices next week if retail demand stays strong.
Planned reductions in beef production for next week, which were announced earlier this week by some packers, also could lend support to beef, sources said.
